summary_paragraph: A female patient with end-stage renal disease, systemic lupus erythematosus, and antiphospholipid syndrome was admitted for dizziness, unsteady gait, and confusion. She had a markedly elevated potassium level of 7.0 without typical symptoms of hyperkalemia. A head CT showed no acute abnormalities. She underwent hemodialysis, which normalized her potassium and resolved her symptoms. The dizziness and confusion were attributed to an acute exacerbation of chronic issues, likely related to atypical migraine. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to continue dialysis, follow up with her PCP, complete an outpatient MRCP, and consider formal cognitive testing. Her medications were continued without changes, and she was advised to hold labetalol on dialysis mornings.
